title: Equivalent Lumped Element Model for Electromigration Considering Thermal Effects
problem: Traditional physics-based electromigration (EM) analysis using partial differential equations (PDEs) is computationally intensive, particularly in multi-physics scenarios with thermal coupling.
motivation: To forecast EM-induced stress under coupled electro-thermomechanical effects with significant computational speedup by leveraging lumped element equivalent circuits.
method: Self-consistent lumped element modeling framework leveraging equivalence between electrical behavior and stress evolution; embedded controlled sources model thermomechanical interactions driven by temperature gradients; threshold-activated switching dynamically reconfigures circuit topology for void nucleation and post-voiding phases; adaptive non-uniform spatial discretization enhances computational efficiency. Fully compatible with standard SPICE solvers.
key_novelty: Lumped element equivalent circuit approach for EM modeling with explicit electro-thermomechanical coupling, enabling SPICE simulation.
contributions: Self-consistent lumped element modeling framework for EM analysis
Embedded controlled sources for thermomechanical interaction modeling
Threshold-activated switching for void nucleation and post-voiding transitions
50× speedup vs FEM for small interconnects, 3.11× over conventional equivalent circuits
limitations: The model is specialized for EM analysis and may require significant adaptation for other coupled physics simulations.
